reviews.review: I just play a little bit

Like any long-running MMO, it can be a little daunting to new players with how many different things there are to do, but the 3rd-person-shooter gameplay and movement mechanics at the core of the game still feel awesome and rewarding even after 1600 hours of spin-dashing around and beating up space goons. 

My personal favorite mechanic is the "Mods" system, which lets you find augments for your Warframes (for those totally new, Warframes are character classes, with their own unique set of 4 abilities, but the gimmick is you find blueprints and craft them the same way you do with weapons) and weapons- anything from "Deal  more of a certain damage type" to "Make your Warframe's abilities larger" to "Shoot/Attack X% faster" to the more unique "Deal more damage, but fire SLOWER" or "Your Warframe's abilities are X% stronger, but are X% SHORTER duration," which really lets you customize how you want your Warframes and weapons to behave.

Warframe is an amazing F2P game. You must try it. I was never a fan of futuristic shooters but then I came across Warframe. Not only is this masterpiece free, but it looks detailed and fun as well. This is not just a mission based shooter; you'll dive into a world of customization, coordination, and quality content. *DISCLAIMER* Some things might be left out probably because I'm writing this as a MR 8 player and havent fully experienced WF yet. In my defense, i've played enough to know this game is great. 

- Overall gameplay is A+
(gunplay, movement, player community, and the customizations are worthwhile and endless)
- Business model is FAIR. (this is a big one for me)
*some items will take forever to farm for (Vauban Prime grrr) but you'll aquire the necessary parts for most items after a few days of playing

Why do I keep saying this game is "fun"? What makes this game so damn fun is that there are a bunch of things to do. One of the main goals in this game are to rank up your Mastery Rank, which is your player's overall level of experience. You do this by getting new items and ranking them up to level 30. You can do this by FARMING for items. This game is all about enjoying Warframe's farming-oriented gameplay with friends. If you don't like farming, this game might just convice you to have fun while doing so (if you hate farming this game maaay not be for you, but still TRY IT). But you farm a lot in WF. A lot. Most of the time, you get some decent items and you (more or less) feel rewarded from your farming sessions. To touch more on the variety of content, most of the time in the game you'll be killing AI and completing missions (farming). It doesn't end there. There is a Team Deathmatch, CTF, and FFA mode called "Conclave". Visit this area of the game once you've got some kickass gear. It still doesn't end there. You then have a soccer/handball like sports mode called Lunaro. Its FUN. This is all in addition to the main kill-everything portion of the game. A little more on gameplay. You, as a player, can control different warframes once you build them through gained parts and items. Each warframe is its own character and playing as these warframes is what makes this game stand out to me. Its freaking fun, man. Its not just an average go out and shoot things - its go out, use your abilities to kill, support, or make life easier, aaand shoot things. The ability mechanic in this game looks spectacular.

Honestly though, if I had to point out Warframe's biggest flaw (in my opinion), it would be the learning curve. A new player can't do much without help from Youtube, the awesome player community, or many of the great (currently recruiting clans). A possible solution would be is to let DE (the devs) know how little information the tutorial provides us in comparison to most of the games content. And for argument's sake, im not asking DE to jam up the tutorial with walls of text info people probably with skip, im only asking that DE make this game easier to "get into". My point is, the game isn't going to spoonfeed you its higher level content. You will be (sort-of) forced into talking to people and going on missions/quests with others. MAKE SURE YOU JOIN AN ACTIVE CLAN. Be social in WF, it helps a bunch. By being social, talk (literally type out your questions) to your squad/clan mates. I can't stress this enough.

Bottom Line: One of the best games I've ever played. 10x better with friends. I recommend this to anyone with a capable computer, just because its loads of fun.

Warframe is basically a space themed mmo, but without the quests and massive array of NPC's and areas you'll find in other mmo's. 

You're not likely to see a more beautifully rendered worldspace than the one in Warframe. The forests feel lush and aive (even with some wild animals that have a big impact on combat); the asteroid base is dark and eerie, with a strong industrial theme; you get the idea.  The movements are wonderfully fluid and natural as well. In the tutorial there's a line "A Tenno should flow like water across the battlefield", and that's no exaggeration: you can easily run across the field, leap to (and continue running along) a wall, then drop back to the ground without hitch or pause. 

Sadly, the beauty is only skin deep. There's no rich story or questline propelling you through the worlds, just an endless grind for better gear (so you can kill tougher stuff and get even better gear), and prestige/ranking. There are several quests, but they're basically just bundles of missions to complete and don't really change the world (though some do grant you extra abilities or unlock certain areas). 

Even the introduction is skimpy, covering just basic movement and the few different weapon types you can start off with. The optional in-game guides aren't much help either, focusing more on what you can do with a feature than on how to use it. There are even several topics that aren't covered in-game at all (e.g. damage types, weapon stats, defenses). It's definitely not for inexperienced players. Thankfully the wikia page for it is very thorough. Just plan on spending a few hours (at least) reading about the game before you stop constantly thinking "what the *@#$ is happening, now?"

Secondly, the multiplayer part is virtually inescapable. There are a few mission [b]types[/b] that are virtually impossible without other players (or ridiculously overpowered single player). And these aren't like raid bosses where you face a big challenge for big rewards, no these are regular missions where you have to accomplish multiple goals simultaneously (e.g. capture and hold 4 separate points on a map, or defend one point while looting enemy drops for fuel; both against endless and large swarms of enemies) for slightly better-than-average rewards. 

The worst part of all, though, is the way it's monetized. As a free-to-play game, you'd expect strong incentives to spend real money (special gear, bonuses, graphical goodies, etc.), but you can't get anything in warframe without either spending real money or grinding for hours and days (acceptable for extra-special stuff, not for basic upgrades). Even your inventory space is limited unless you spend $$$. 

Overall, if you don't mind spending time studying and grinding so you can play as a space ninja, you might enjoy this game.
